title: Power Pages: first-class support for Power Platform connector APIs
summary: Hold: the data-policy PowerShell entry is not a runnable command in the form shown. The licensing paragraph also treats existing Power Pages capacity requirements as unpublished, although Microsoft documents capacity-based licensing for website visitors; only additional terms specific to native connector APIs remain unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans native Power Pages connectors to enterprise systems such as SQL, SAP and Oracle.
claims.quote: Native connectors support through Power Pages will allow organizations to securely connect their websites/portals directly to enterprise systems such as SQL, SAP, and Oracle

claims.claim: The planned capability avoids building or maintaining a custom integration layer.
claims.quote: without building or maintaining custom integration layers.

claims.claim: The roadmap highlights regulated enterprise customers with data behind corporate firewalls.
claims.quote: This capability is especially valuable for regulated and enterprise customers such as banking and financial services, who need to surface data from systems hosted behind corporate firewalls.

claims.claim: The design uses the Power Platform on-premises data gateway and connector framework.
claims.quote: By leveraging the Power Platform on-premises data gateway and connector framework

claims.claim: The roadmap describes server-side logic interacting with on-premises data sources.
claims.quote: while gaining the flexibility to build server-side logic that can interact with on-premises data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap promises consistent security and governance with existing Power Platform policies.
claims.quote: Customers benefit from consistent security, governance, and compliance with existing Power Platform policies

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: General availability is listed for June CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2027"

claims.claim: Preview is listed for March CY2027.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The default state of the planned native connector API capability is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector APIs" "enable"; "Power Pages" "native connectors" "connector APIs" licensing default. Read roadmap and Server logic overview; neither states the planned native connector capability's default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing terms specific to the planned native connector API capability have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages licensing native Power Platform connectors on premises gateway premium connector licensing. Opened Power Pages licensing and Power Platform licensing FAQs; neither specifies additional native connector API terms.

claims.claim: Whether Power Pages capacity applies is to be confirmed when Microsoft publishes the terms.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of Cost and licensing with: "Any additional premium connector licensing, gateway hosting charges or capacity charges specific to native connector APIs are not yet published." Existing Power Pages website licensing is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq#power-pages; do not describe its applicability as unpublished.

claims.claim: Data policy creation is reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote:
select Security, and then on the Security pane, select Data and privacy.
3. On the Data protection and privacy page, select Data policy.
4. Select an existing policy on the command bar and then select Edit policy, or select New Policy

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy (Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell) is the runnable PowerShell call for the data-policy row.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy

Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api.call and the corresponding rendered table code with "New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy". The module name is metadata, not a parenthesized argument to execute; the reference documents -NewPolicy as the required policy-object parameter.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering is configured within a data policy through Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.quote: The Endpoint configurable column on the Prebuilt Connectors page in Data Policies indicates whether the endpoint filtering capability is supported for the connector.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations with TenantId, PolicyName and NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations creates policy endpoint configurations.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is a preview feature.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering evaluates static designer endpoints rather than dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules don't apply to environment variables, custom inputs, or any endpoint dynamically created at runtime. Only static endpoints are evaluated in the app, flow, or chatbot designers.

claims.claim: The connector must have Endpoint configurable set to Yes to expose the endpoint-filtering UI.
claims.quote: If the value of the Endpoint configurable column is Yes, you can use this capability by right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not confirm that the two general data-policy controls govern the planned native Power Pages connector APIs.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector" "on-premises" "policies". Opened Data policies, Connector action control and Connector endpoint filtering; read Advanced connector policies excerpts. None identifies native Power Pages connector APIs as covered.

claims.claim: No Power Pages-specific UI or automation control for native connector APIs is yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector APIs" "enable"; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" "pac pages" "PowerShell". Read admin API and CLI search results and Server logic overview; found only controls for other capabilities.

claims.claim: No Learn documentation for the planned native connector API feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native connectors" "connector APIs" licensing default; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" "enable". Results concerned connector catalogs, server logic, MCP, or other products, not this planned capability.

claims.claim: Per-visitor authorisation for the planned native connector API data is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector APIs" permissions connection identity supported operations admin site settings PowerShell Dataverse. Opened Server logic overview and Power Pages security; these document general and Dataverse access, not native connector authorisation.

claims.claim: Connection identity and per-visitor delegation for the planned native connector capability are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native connectors" "identity"; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" permissions connection identity supported operations admin site settings PowerShell Dataverse. Read Power Pages security and Server logic overview; no native connector identity model found.

claims.claim: Supported operations for the planned native connector capability are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector APIs" permissions connection identity supported operations admin site settings PowerShell Dataverse. Opened Server logic overview; its methods describe general server logic, not the planned native connector operation set.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports POST for sending data to external systems.
claims.quote: POST | function post() { } | Create records or send new data. | Commonly used to insert new records into Dataverse or send data to external systems.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PUT for replacing or updating records.
claims.quote: PUT | function put() { } | Replace or update records. | Updates or replaces an entire record or dataset.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PATCH for partial record updates.
claims.quote: PATCH | function patch() { } | Updates part of a record (upsert). | Performs a partial update of existing data without replacing the entire record.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports DELETE for removing data from external systems.
claims.quote: DELETE | function del() { } | Delete records or fields. | Removes records or data from Dataverse or an external system.

claims.claim: Power Pages sites are available to internal users by default.
claims.quote: By default, all Power Pages sites are available to users who are internal to your organization.

claims.where: Governance controls; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Public site visibility allows anonymous Internet access.
claims.quote: The public setting makes the site accessible to everyone over the Internet anonymously or to users authenticated through identity providers.
